# Sweden — Builder Mode

Builder-mode derivation constraint: builder-mode content derives strictly from `evidence.md`, `signals.md`, `trust-dimensions.md`, `metadata.md`, and `profile.md`.

This file translates the normalized Sweden profile into builder-facing interpretation.

This file provides structural interpretation only. It does not assign routing authority, readiness tiers, Atlas surfaces, jurisdiction rankings, or deployment suitability.

## Digital Governance Coordination Environment

For builder interpretation, Sweden reads as a Nordic digital-governance coordination environment centered on DIGG Ena, Sweden Connect interoperability, Swedish eIDAS node participation, Min Myndighetspost messaging infrastructure, dataportal.se registry continuity, DIGITAL programme participation, and Single Digital Gateway linkage. The current normalized layers show DIGG coordinating a joint national digital infrastructure for information exchange, e-identification, e-signatures, and cross-border interoperability surfaces rather than isolated public-service tools. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on national digital identity coordination and EU-linked interoperability continuity rather than on a fully standalone domestic identity perimeter.

## Settlement Infrastructure Environment

For builder interpretation, Sweden reads as a central-bank settlement modernization environment structured through Riksbank settlement governance, RIX-RTGS large-value settlement infrastructure, RIX-INST instant settlement infrastructure, TIPS linkage participation, and the e-krona research programme. The current normalized layers show a dual settlement structure spanning large-value and instant-payment functions, with Swish settlement migration into RIX-INST preserved as a visible modernization step. The same layers place instant settlement inside a wider Eurosystem-linked platform environment through TIPS and preserve the e-krona as a continuing CBDC research and preparedness surface rather than a finalized issuance path. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on settlement modernization continuity inside hybrid domestic-Eurosystem coordination.

## Telecommunications Standards Environment

For builder interpretation, Sweden reads as a telecommunications standards-participation jurisdiction anchored in Ericsson standardisation continuity, 3GPP participation, ETSI-linked coordination, PTS spectrum governance, and PTS trust-services supervision under the eIDAS framework. The current normalized layers show Ericsson as a durable standards-participation surface based in Sweden rather than as a routing-control claim. They also preserve PTS as the communications authority responsible for spectrum governance continuity and trust-services supervision inside the documented digital-governance setting. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on standards participation and telecommunications governance continuity without inferring telecom hierarchy or routing authority.

## Research Network and Compute Environment

For builder interpretation, Sweden reads as a research-network federation platform structured through Sunet national research-network continuity, SunetC encrypted backbone infrastructure, NORDUnet participation, NAISS compute coordination, and EuroHPC Arrhenius hosting at Linköping University. The current normalized layers show Sunet operating, maintaining, and developing the university network across higher education, research, identity services, and IT-security functions, while SunetC preserves encrypted transmission, redundancy, and dedicated connectivity options across the academic backbone. NORDUnet participation links this national network surface into standing Nordic cooperation, and NAISS together with Arrhenius hosting preserves a research-compute environment attached to wider European compute participation. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on federated research-network and compute coordination continuity rather than a sovereign compute-stack classification.

## Exchange and Internet Infrastructure Environment

For builder interpretation, Sweden reads as a neutral exchange-layer infrastructure participant centered on Netnod exchange continuity, Netnod DNS, root-server, and time-service infrastructure, .se registry governance through the Swedish Internet Foundation, and bounded operator-hosted compute participation through EcoDataCenter. The current normalized layers show Netnod as a neutral and independent internet infrastructure organization supporting interconnection together with DNS, transport, root-server, and time functions. They also preserve registry governance continuity through .se and .nu administration and add EcoDataCenter as an operator-hosted compute surface without changing the documented absence of a sovereign hyperscale classification. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on exchange neutrality, registry stewardship, and bounded operator-hosted infrastructure participation.

## Energy and Grid Integration Environment

For builder interpretation, Sweden reads as a Nordic electricity-market integration jurisdiction structured through Svenska kraftnät transmission coordination, Nordic electricity-market participation, Aurora Line interconnector participation, Konti-Skan Connect linkage, and a multi-source generation environment. The current normalized layers show Svenska kraftnät coordinating the national grid, balancing production and consumption, and maintaining a transmission system connected to neighboring countries. They also preserve market coupling, Finland linkage through Aurora Line, Denmark linkage through Konti-Skan renewal, and a generation environment combining hydropower, wind, solar, biomass, and nuclear-related inputs. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on cross-border Nordic electricity-system continuity rather than a nationally closed energy perimeter.

## Cybersecurity and Civil Contingency Environment

For builder interpretation, Sweden reads as a civil-contingency and cyber-incident coordination environment structured through Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency coordination, CERT-SE national CSIRT continuity, EU CSIRTs Network participation, FIRST participation, TF-CSIRT participation, and National Coordination Centre cybersecurity linkage. The current normalized layers show a standing preparedness environment spanning crisis coordination, major accidents, and consequences-of-war functions rather than episodic response-only activity. They also preserve CERT-SE as a centralized national incident-management and prevention-support surface for essential services and critical infrastructure together with repeated participation in EU and international coordination structures. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on civil-contingency and cyber-coordination continuity embedded within EU and international cooperation systems.

## Battery and Advanced Manufacturing Environment

For builder interpretation, Sweden reads as a battery-industrial ecosystem anchor structured through Northvolt Ett battery-industrial infrastructure, the BASE battery research alliance, government battery-plant coordination, and European battery value-chain participation. The current normalized layers show Skellefteå as a visible large-scale battery-manufacturing anchor tied to renewable electricity inputs, while BASE preserves a coordinated alliance spanning universities, RISE, manufacturers, automotive actors, suppliers, and recycling-related participants. Government coordination of large battery-plant establishment links this industrial surface to the wider automotive transition and European battery-industry setting. These conditions support a builder-facing reading centered on battery-industrial anchoring and research-alliance continuity without extending into a semiconductor fabrication-stack profile.

## Structural Constraints for Builders

The current Sweden builder-mode reading also carries clear structural limits. The normalized layers do not document a sovereign hyperscale compute stack. They do not document a semiconductor fabrication stack classification beyond the preserved battery-industrial and telecom-manufacturing surfaces. Major continuity layers depend on Nordic electricity-market coupling, Eurosystem settlement linkage through TIPS, and EU digital-identity interoperability structures. The current normalized layers also preserve long north-south infrastructure distribution and coordination distance as structural conditions across nationally important network, industrial, and energy assets. These conditions define the documented builder-mode perimeter without being treated as weaknesses or readiness judgments.

## Builder Mode Summary Statement

Sweden appears in builder mode as a Nordic digital-governance coordination jurisdiction, telecommunications-standards participation environment, research-network federation platform, settlement modernization surface, battery-industrial ecosystem anchor, and cross-border electricity-market integration participant embedded within EU, Nordic, and Baltic institutional systems.

# Sweden — Signals Layer

Signal derivation constraint: signals derive strictly from `evidence.md`. This file does not assign routing authority, topology placement, readiness tiers, Atlas surfaces, jurisdiction rankings, or deployment suitability.

## Strategic Position Signals

- DIGG's Ena coordination role, Netnod's neutral exchange infrastructure, Ericsson's standards-participation surface, Sunet's national research-network role, and Sweden's documented EU, Nordic, and Baltic institutional participation together signal a distributed Nordic coordination surface spanning digital identity, telecom standards participation, research networking, and grid-interconnection structures rather than a single centralized national stack.
- Svenska kraftnät's transmission role and cross-border interconnection evidence reinforce a signal of national infrastructure continuity organized through connected systems rather than a closed domestic perimeter.
- The evidence supports a coordination-and-interoperability signal rooted in digital infrastructure, research networking, interconnection, and regional institutional attachment, but it does not support a standalone autonomy classification detached from EU, Nordic, and Baltic frameworks.

## Digital Governance and Identity Signals

- DIGG's responsibility for Ena, e-identification coordination, Sweden Connect, and the Swedish eIDAS node signals a nationally visible digital identity and interoperability surface organized inside documented EU framework participation.
- The combined presence of Min Myndighetspost, dataportal.se, and DIGG's digital-services coordination signals continuity across public-service messaging, data access, and information-exchange infrastructure rather than isolated service points.
- DIGG's roles in the DIGITAL programme, the Single Digital Gateway, and eIDAS participation signal national digital identity interoperability continuity inside EU-linked governance structures rather than a fully standalone domestic identity regime.

## Financial Infrastructure and CBDC Signals

- Riksbank evidence on RIX-RTGS and RIX-INST signals a central-bank settlement environment spanning both large-value and instant-payment infrastructure.
- RIX-INST's real-time settlement role, its linkage to the Eurosystem's TIPS platform, and the migration of Swish settlement into RIX-INST together signal continuing settlement modernization within a central-bank-operated infrastructure layer.
- The e-krona programme signals ongoing CBDC research continuity and preparedness activity, while the evidence does not support a claim of completed issuance or finalized deployment path.

## Telecommunications and Standards Signals

- Ericsson's documented participation and leadership in 3GPP-related standardisation work signals telecommunications standards participation continuity anchored in Sweden rather than network-routing authority.
- PTS spectrum governance materials signal an institutional spectrum-management surface tied to secure, efficient frequency use and continuing telecom development, including 5G-related assignments where demand exceeds available spectrum.
- DIGG's eIDAS materials, which place trust-services supervision at PTS, signal a linked telecom-and-trust-services governance layer rather than an isolated spectrum-only regulatory role.
- The evidence supports standards participation and telecom-governance continuity, but it does not support a routing-core or telecom-hierarchy classification.

## Research Network and Compute Signals

- Sunet's role operating, maintaining, and developing the university data network signals a nationally coordinated research-network environment spanning higher education, research, identity infrastructure, and IT-security services.
- SunetC's encrypted transmission capacity, redundancy, and dedicated point-to-point and cross-border connectivity options signal durable research-network continuity rather than a limited campus-only network surface.
- Sweden's participation in NORDUnet signals formal regional research-network attachment beyond the domestic national backbone.
- NAISS and EuroHPC Arrhenius hosting at Linköping University together signal national research-compute coordination continuity linking domestic academic infrastructure with wider European compute participation.

## Exchange and Data Infrastructure Signals

- Netnod's neutral exchange role, combined with its DNS, time, and root-server services, signals neutral Nordic exchange-layer infrastructure continuity rather than a purely commercial interconnection surface.
- The Swedish Internet Foundation's responsibility for .se and operation of .nu signals registry governance continuity tied to stable and secure national internet infrastructure administration.
- EcoDataCenter's documented hosting environment signals bounded operator-hosted data-centre continuity within Sweden, while the evidence does not support a sovereign hyperscale classification.
- Taken together, the evidence supports exchange neutrality, internet-infrastructure stewardship, and operator-hosted data continuity without supporting a separate national hyperscale-sovereignty signal.

## Energy and Grid Integration Signals

- Svenska kraftnät's transmission-system role and balancing responsibility signal a nationally coordinated electricity-transmission environment attached to continuous operational oversight.
- Documented Nordic electricity-market coupling and cross-border connections signal cross-border Nordic grid-integration continuity rather than a fully self-contained national power environment.
- Aurora Line and Konti-Skan Connect together signal continuing reinforcement of Sweden's interconnector-based transmission links with Finland and Denmark.
- The documented mix of hydro, wind, solar, biomass, and nuclear-related inputs signals a multi-source generation structure feeding into the transmission and interconnection layer without implying energy autonomy ranking.

## Cybersecurity and Civil Contingency Signals

- Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency evidence signals civil-contingency coordination continuity across crisis, accident, and war-consequence preparedness functions.
- CERT-SE's national CSIRT role signals a centralized cyber-incident coordination surface for essential services and critical infrastructure rather than a fragmented sector-by-sector response environment.
- CERT-SE participation in the EU CSIRTs Network, European Government CERTs, FIRST, and TF-CSIRT signals cross-border cyber-coordination continuity anchored in both national and international information-sharing structures.
- The National Coordination Centre materials signal continued linkage between domestic cybersecurity coordination and EU research-and-innovation participation.

## Battery and Advanced Manufacturing Signals

- Northvolt Ett signals visible battery-industrial infrastructure continuity through large-scale battery manufacturing capacity located in northern Sweden and tied to renewable electricity inputs.
- BASE signals a coordinated national battery-research alliance spanning universities, RISE, manufacturers, automotive actors, suppliers, and recycling-related participants across the battery value chain.
- Government coordination of battery-plant establishment signals institutional support for battery-industrial buildout within broader automotive-transition and European battery-value-chain frameworks.
- The evidence supports battery-industrial coordination continuity, but it does not support a complete domestic semiconductor-fabrication-stack signal.

## EU and Nordic Corridor Integration Signals

- Sweden's EU membership and DIGG's DIGITAL programme and Single Digital Gateway roles together signal institutional continuity inside EU digital-governance and coordination frameworks.
- Nordic cooperation materials and Sunet's participation in NORDUnet signal multi-layer Nordic coordination continuity across both governmental and research-network structures.
- CBSS membership and the Stockholm-based secretariat signal Baltic Sea institutional participation continuity tied to regional coordination structures.
- Trafikverket's ScanMed corridor participation signals transport-corridor continuity linking Swedish infrastructure into wider north-south European freight frameworks.
- Taken together, the evidence supports multi-layer Nordic-EU corridor integration continuity rather than a standalone national corridor classification.

## Constraint Boundary Signals

- The evidence does not support a sovereign hyperscale compute stack signal beyond the documented exchange, research-compute, and operator-hosted data-centre surfaces.
- Nordic electricity-market coupling and cross-border interconnectors signal structural dependence on shared regional electricity-market and transmission arrangements rather than a fully isolated national power system.
- RIX-INST's linkage to the Eurosystem's TIPS platform signals continued settlement modernization inside a wider European settlement infrastructure dependency.
- DIGG's eIDAS, Sweden Connect, and Single Digital Gateway roles signal that digital-identity interoperability continuity depends in part on wider EU framework participation rather than on a purely domestic identity perimeter.
- The evidence does not support a complete domestic semiconductor fabrication stack signal.
- The documented long north-south infrastructure distribution, together with major northern industrial and energy assets and nationally distributed network redundancy, signals distance and coordination burdens as structural conditions, but not a ranking variable or topology inference basis.

## Signals Summary Statement

Sweden's evidence-derived signals describe a Nordic digital-governance, telecommunications-standards participation, research-network coordination, grid-integration, and battery-industrial infrastructure jurisdiction embedded within EU, Nordic, and Baltic institutional systems. The signals indicate continuity across identity interoperability, central-bank settlement modernization, research-compute coordination, neutral exchange infrastructure, cross-border electricity integration, cyber-incident coordination, and battery-industry organization without assigning readiness tiers, routing authority, or topology placement.

- EU institutional participation indicates durable attachment to European governance channels rather than a nationally isolated coordination environment.
- Nordic cooperation materials and NORDUnet participation indicate that Sweden's governmental and research-network layers are both linked to standing Nordic structures.
- CBSS participation indicates Baltic coordination continuity carried through a formal regional organization with secretariat presence in Stockholm.
- ScanMed freight-corridor participation indicates transport-continuity attachment to wider north-south European freight structures.
- DIGITAL programme participation reinforces that digital-governance continuity is also embedded within EU programme-linked coordination channels.

## Constraint Boundary Dimension

- The source layers do not document a sovereign hyperscale compute stack, which bounds compute and cloud trust claims beyond exchange, research-compute, and operator-hosted data-centre surfaces.
- Nordic electricity-market coupling and interconnector dependence bound the energy dimension within shared regional market and transmission arrangements rather than a fully isolated national system.
- TIPS linkage bounds settlement-modernization continuity within hybrid domestic-Eurosystem coordination rather than a wholly domestic instant-settlement perimeter.
- eIDAS, Sweden Connect, and Single Digital Gateway participation bound digital-identity continuity inside wider EU interoperability structures.
- The source layers do not document a complete domestic semiconductor fabrication stack, which limits advanced-manufacturing trust claims to the documented battery-industrial and telecom-manufacturing surfaces.
- Sweden's long north-south infrastructure distribution and major northern industrial and energy assets indicate coordination-distance burdens as structural boundary conditions without supporting ranking or topology inference.

## Trust Dimensions Summary Statement

Sweden appears in the trust layer as a Nordic digital-governance, telecommunications-standards participation, research-network coordination, grid-integration, and battery-industrial infrastructure jurisdiction embedded within EU, Nordic, and Baltic institutional systems. The documented trust dimensions indicate continuity across institutional coordination, identity interoperability, settlement modernization, standards participation, research-compute federation, neutral internet infrastructure, cross-border electricity integration, cyber-incident coordination, and battery-industry organization without assigning readiness tiers, routing authority, or deployment eligibility.

# Sweden — Evidence Layer

## Strategic Position

- DIGG states that it is responsible for Ena, the name of Sweden's digital infrastructure, and that it coordinates e-identification, e-signatures, public-data access, and cross-border digital-government programs.
- Svenska kraftnät states that it maintains and develops the Swedish national grid, balances production and consumption, and operates a transmission system with international connections.
- Netnod states that it is a neutral and independent internet infrastructure organisation based in Sweden and that it operates the largest internet exchange in the Nordics alongside DNS, time, transport, and root-server services.
- Ericsson materials place the company's global headquarters in Stockholm and document Swedish participation in telecommunications standardisation work through ETSI and 3GPP-related leadership materials.
- Sunet states that it operates, maintains, and develops Sweden's university data network and provides national research-network, identity, and IT-security services linked to higher education and research.
- Government, Nordic-cooperation, CBSS, and Trafikverket materials place Sweden inside EU, Nordic, Baltic Sea, and ScanMed corridor coordination structures without assigning corridor authority or topology role.

Sources:
- Digg, "Management and coordination"
- Svenska kraftnät, "Map of the national grid"
- Svenska kraftnät, "Operations and Electricity Markets"
- Netnod, "About Netnod"
- Ericsson, company-facts and standardisation materials surfaced via official site search results
- Sunet, "About Sunet"
- Government.se, "Sweden in the EU" materials surfaced via official site search results
- Nordic cooperation, official-cooperation materials surfaced via official site search results
- CBSS, "Member States"
- Trafikverket, "ScanMed Freight corridor"

## Digital Governance and Identity Infrastructure

- DIGG states that it is responsible for Ena, Sweden's digital infrastructure, and that its work includes leading and coordinating a joint digital infrastructure for information exchange.
- DIGG states that it coordinates e-identification and e-signatures nationally and internationally.
- DIGG states that it is responsible for the Swedish eIDAS single point of contact, Sweden's participation in the eIDAS Cooperation Network, and Sweden Connect, which includes the Swedish eIDAS node, the Technical Framework, and the General Register for secure eID transactions within Sweden.
- DIGG states that eID is used to verify identity online when using services, contacting authorities, and interacting with banks and other digital services.
- DIGG states that it is responsible for Min Myndighetspost and that dataportal.se indexes public and private datasets for broader reuse.
- DIGG states that it is the national coordinator for the DIGITAL programme and for the Single Digital Gateway, linking Swedish digital public-service coordination to EU interoperability structures.

Sources:
- Digg, "Management and coordination"
- Digg, "eID"
- Digg, "Digital services"
- Government.se, "The Agency for Digital Government" materials surfaced via official site search results

## Financial Infrastructure and CBDC Exploration

- Riksbank materials state that the Riksbank is investigating the e-krona as a digital complement to cash and that the technical e-krona project was finalised in 2023.
- The same Riksbank materials state that the e-krona would complement rather than replace cash and that future work is focused on monitoring international CBDC developments, including work on a digital euro.
- Riksbank materials surfaced via official site search results state that the RIX system consists of RIX-RTGS for large-value and aggregated payments and RIX-INST for instant payments.
- Riksbank materials surfaced via official site search results state that RIX-INST settles instant payments between banks in real time, 24 hours a day and all year round in central bank money, using the Eurosystem's TIPS platform.
- Riksbank materials surfaced via official site search results state that clearing organisations such as Bankgirot aggregate large numbers of account payments that are then exchanged in RIX.
- Riksbank materials surfaced via official site search results state that, from March 2024, Swish payments moved to settlement through RIX-INST.

Sources:
- Sveriges Riksbank, "The e-krona – state money in digital form"
- Sveriges Riksbank, "How payments work" materials surfaced via official site search results
- Sveriges Riksbank, "Payments Department" materials surfaced via official site search results
- Sveriges Riksbank, "RIX-INST enables competition and innovation" materials surfaced via official site search results
- Sveriges Riksbank, notice on Swish payments moving to RIX-INST surfaced via official site search results
- Sveriges Riksbank, RIX-INST instructions materials surfaced via official site search results

## Telecommunications and Standards Infrastructure

- Ericsson materials surfaced via official site search results state that the company's global headquarters are in Stockholm and that Sweden has been its base for roughly 150 years.
- Ericsson standardisation materials surfaced via official site search results document participation and leadership in 3GPP standardisation work for 5G releases and identify ETSI as a founding partner of 3GPP.
- PTS presents itself as working for secure and accessible communication for Sweden.
- DIGG's eIDAS materials state that PTS is responsible for supervision under the eIDAS trust-services framework.
- PTS auction materials surfaced via official site search results state that spectrum auctions are used where demand exceeds available spectrum and that assignments are intended to support efficient, secure frequency use and continued technological development including 5G.
- Government digital-policy materials surfaced via official site search results place broadband, digital mail, digital identity, and 5G within Sweden's national digital-policy framework.

Sources:
- Ericsson, company-facts materials surfaced via official site search results
- Ericsson, "Standardization leadership in telecommunications" materials surfaced via official site search results
- Ericsson, "Network standards: from 1G to 6G and beyond" materials surfaced via official site search results
- PTS, homepage
- PTS, auctions materials surfaced via official site search results
- Digg, "eID"
- Government.se, "Digital policy" materials surfaced via official site search results

## Research Network and Compute Infrastructure

- Sunet states that it operates, maintains, and develops Sweden's university data network and serves higher-education institutions and other public organisations linked to research, higher education, and culture.
- Sunet states that it provides identity infrastructure, enhanced IT-security services, and international access to other e-infrastructures and associated resources.
- Sunet states that Sunet CD has 400 Gbit/s transmission capacity, fully encrypted data communication, and redundancy for Swedish higher-education institutions and affiliated cultural organisations.
- Sunet states that SunetC provides nationwide access to the internet and global research networks and can provide dedicated point-to-point and cross-border research-network connections.
- Sunet states that it represents Sweden in NORDUnet, the Nordic cooperation between the region's national research and education networks.
- NAISS materials state that the National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing in Sweden maintains advanced computing, AI, and data services for Swedish research, is hosted by Linköping University, and is funded by the Swedish Research Council for 2023–2026.
- Linköping University and EuroHPC materials state that Linköping University, through NAISS, is hosting the EuroHPC supercomputer Arrhenius for researchers in academia and industry across Europe.

Sources:
- Sunet, "About Sunet"
- Sunet, "The Sunet network"
- NAISS, "About us"
- Linköping University, "Agreement signed – supercomputer Arrhenius to Linköping"
- EuroHPC JU, Sweden/Arrhenius materials surfaced via official site search results

## Internet Exchange and Data Infrastructure

- Netnod states that it provides interconnection services, internet exchanges, time services, DNS services, and root-server operations.
- Netnod states that it was established in 1996 as a neutral and independent internet infrastructure organisation based in Sweden and that it runs the largest internet exchange in the Nordics.
- The Swedish Internet Foundation states that it is responsible for the Swedish top-level domain .se and the operation of the top-level domain .nu and that its charter includes ensuring a strong and secure internet infrastructure in Sweden.
- The Swedish Internet Foundation states that its mission includes promoting stability in Swedish internet infrastructure and the spread of knowledge about the internet and electronic communication.
- Operator materials surfaced via official site search results from EcoDataCenter document Swedish data-centre facilities in Falun and Borlänge and describe a compute-hosting model framed around flexibility, security, sustainability, and minimal climate impact.

Sources:
- Netnod, "About Netnod"
- The Swedish Internet Foundation, "About us"
- The Swedish Internet Foundation, domain materials surfaced via official site search results
- EcoDataCenter, site and location materials surfaced via official site search results

## Energy and Grid Integration Infrastructure

- Svenska kraftnät states that the Swedish national grid consists of approximately 16,000 km of power lines, about 175 substations and switching stations, and connections to other countries.
- Svenska kraftnät states that it is Sweden's electricity system operator and is responsible for balancing production and consumption in real time.
- Svenska kraftnät materials surfaced via official site search results state that the national grid transports electricity from wind, hydro, and nuclear generation into regional and local networks.
- Svenska kraftnät materials surfaced via official site search results place Sweden within the Nordic electricity-market structure, including four bidding areas and day-ahead price formation on the Nordic power exchange.
- Svenska kraftnät states that Aurora Line is a planned new 400 kV interconnector between Messaure in Sweden and Pyhänselkä in Finland, developed with Fingrid and classified as an EU Project of Common Interest.
- Svenska kraftnät states that Konti-Skan Connect is renewing the HVDC connection between Lindome in Sweden and Vester Hassing in Denmark together with Energinet.
- The Swedish Energy Agency states that Sweden's energy system includes hydropower, wind power, solar, biomass, and nuclear-related inputs and that the system is undergoing transformation with conversion losses and changing generation shares.

Sources:
- Svenska kraftnät, "Map of the national grid"
- Svenska kraftnät, "Operations and Electricity Markets"
- Svenska kraftnät, "Aurora Line"
- Svenska kraftnät, "Konti-Skan Connect"
- Svenska kraftnät, activity and control-room materials surfaced via official site search results
- Swedish Energy Agency, "How the energy system works" materials surfaced via official site search results
- Swedish Energy Agency, "Energy Transformation"

## Cybersecurity and Civil Contingency Coordination

- Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency materials surfaced via official site search results state that the agency is responsible for helping society prepare for major accidents, crises, and the consequences of war.
- The agency's English materials include digital security and business-preparedness guidance within a wider civil-defence and resilience mandate.
- CERT-SE states that it is Sweden's national CSIRT supporting Swedish society in managing and preventing IT-security incidents, with priority for essential services and critical infrastructure.
- CERT-SE states that it reacts to incidents, coordinates large-scale incident management, and supports affected organisations in mitigating and restoring function.
- CERT-SE states that it cooperates with agencies in the Swedish National Cyber Security Centre and serves as a contact point for corresponding functions in other countries.
- CERT-SE lists participation in the EU CSIRTs Network, European Government CERTs group, FIRST, TF-CSIRT/Trusted Introducer, and other national and international information-sharing forums.
- Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency materials surfaced via official site search results state that the Swedish National Coordination Centre for cybersecurity research and innovation enables EU funding access for Swedish research institutes, companies, and public authorities.

Sources:
- Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency, homepage
- Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency materials surfaced via official site search results
- CERT-SE, homepage
- Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency, National Coordination Centre materials surfaced via official site search results

## Advanced Manufacturing and Battery Infrastructure

- Northvolt states that Northvolt Ett in Skellefteå is a lithium-ion battery gigafactory in northern Sweden and describes it as Europe's first homegrown gigafactory.
- Northvolt states that Northvolt Ett is powered by renewable electricity and that the site includes large-scale industrial battery production capacity in Sweden.
- Vinnova states that Batteries Sweden (BASE) is Sweden's battery alliance for long-term battery research, intended to strengthen the Swedish battery research community across the entire battery value chain.
- Vinnova states that BASE links Uppsala University, Chalmers, KTH, RISE, cell manufacturers, automotive actors, material developers, software and hardware suppliers, and recycling companies.
- Government materials surfaced via official site search results state that the government instructed Business Sweden to coordinate efforts to set up large battery plants as part of the automotive industry's green transition.
- The current source set documents battery-industrial coordination and research infrastructure, but does not document a complete domestic semiconductor fabrication stack.

Sources:
- Northvolt, "Northvolt Ett"
- Vinnova, "Batteries Sweden (BASE), Phase 2"
- Government.se, battery-value-chain and battery-plant coordination materials surfaced via official site search results

## EU and Nordic Corridor Integration

- Government materials surfaced via official site search results state that Sweden is an EU member state and that the Government represents Sweden in the European Council and the Council of the European Union.
- DIGG states that it is the national coordinator for the DIGITAL programme and for the Single Digital Gateway, adding EU institutional linkage to Swedish digital-governance infrastructure.
- Nordic-cooperation materials surfaced via official site search results state that the Nordic Council of Ministers is the official body for intergovernmental cooperation in the Nordic region and that Sweden is part of that structure.
- Sunet states that Sweden participates in NORDUnet, linking Swedish research-network infrastructure to formal Nordic network cooperation.
- CBSS states that Sweden is one of the member states of the Council of the Baltic Sea States and that the organisation's secretariat is based in Stockholm.
- Trafikverket states that Sweden is part of the ScanMed freight corridor, linking Stockholm and Malmö through Copenhagen, Hamburg, Innsbruck, Verona, and Palermo within the EU freight-corridor framework.

Sources:
- Government.se, "Sweden in the EU" materials surfaced via official site search results
- Digg, "Management and coordination"
- Nordic cooperation, official-cooperation materials surfaced via official site search results
- Sunet, "About Sunet"
- CBSS, "Member States"
- CBSS, secretariat and structure materials surfaced via official site search results
- Trafikverket, "ScanMed Freight corridor"

## Constraints and Structural Limitations

- DIGG and Government materials place Swedish digital identity, eIDAS interoperability, DIGITAL coordination, and the Single Digital Gateway inside wider EU digital-governance frameworks rather than a fully standalone national regime.
- Riksbank materials place payment modernisation in relation to the Eurosystem's TIPS platform and continuing CBDC monitoring tied in part to broader European digital-currency developments.
- Svenska kraftnät materials document cross-border transmission links and Nordic power-market coupling, indicating that parts of Sweden's electricity-market operation are structurally tied to neighbouring systems and shared market mechanisms.
- The current source set documents research networking, NAISS, EuroHPC participation, exchange infrastructure, and operator-hosted data-centre capacity, but does not document an independent Swedish sovereign hyperscale compute stack.
- The current source set documents battery-industrial and telecom-manufacturing coordination surfaces, but does not document a complete domestic semiconductor fabrication stack.
- The current source set documents nationally important infrastructure across a long north-south geography, including nationwide research-network redundancy and major northern industrial and energy assets, but does not provide a separate official basis for treating geography itself as an institutional ranking variable.

Sources:
- Digg, "Management and coordination"
- Digg, "eID"
- Government.se, digital-policy and EU-participation materials surfaced via official site search results
- Sveriges Riksbank, e-krona and RIX/TIPS materials surfaced via official site search results
- Svenska kraftnät, "Map of the national grid"
- Svenska kraftnät, "Aurora Line"
- Svenska kraftnät, "Konti-Skan Connect"
- Sunet, "About Sunet"
- NAISS, "About us"
- EuroHPC JU and Linköping University Arrhenius materials
- Netnod, "About Netnod"
- Northvolt, "Northvolt Ett"
- Vinnova, "Batteries Sweden (BASE), Phase 2"

## Summary

The current source set documents Sweden as a Nordic digital-governance, telecommunications, research-network, low-carbon energy, and Baltic/Nordic corridor-integration jurisdiction embedded within EU and Nordic institutional systems. The evidence places Swedish digital identity coordination, payment modernisation, exchange infrastructure, research networking, high-performance computing, grid interconnection, civil-contingency cyber functions, and battery-industrial coordination inside linked national, Nordic, Baltic, and EU frameworks without assigning readiness tiers or routing authority.
